title: Why You See Stars When You Stand Up

sections.name: Why You See Stars When You Stand Up
lines: Stand up too fast, and everything goes dark and sparkly.
When you stand, gravity pulls blood down, into your legs.
So for a moment, less blood gets pumped up to your head.
Sensors in your neck notice the drop, and tell your heart to beat faster, and your vessels to tighten.
But that takes a few seconds. Meanwhile, your brain and eyes run a little low on oxygen.
So your vision fades, and you see stars. It's called a head rush.
Stand up slowly, and your body has time to catch up.
